name: conjure fey
lore:
### On the Calling of the Sidhe: Conjure Fey

To summon a denizen of the Courts is to invite beautiful chaos into the mundane. As the incantation peaks, the air thickens with the scent of crushed mint and ozone. To the caster, the Weave feels like a silken ribbon pulled taut—not the rigid geometry of common wizardry, but a vibrating, living pulse that tastes of wild honey and cold iron on the tongue.

Visually, the magic manifests as a shimmering fracture in reality, weeping iridescent dew and shedding autumn leaves that vanish before hitting the earth. From this prismatic rift, the Fey emerges wreathed in starlight, their presence a heavy weight of ancient, alien curiosity.

Legend attributes this discovery to Caelen the Mute, a hermit of the Whispering Woods. It is said he did not study tomes but hummed a melody taught by the wind. When the first dryad stepped through the veil, Caelen found his voice, though he spoke only the sibilant tongue of the Sidhe thereafter.

*A Word of Caution:* The Fey are not servants; they are guests with teeth. Bind them with respect, or risk becoming the punchline of a century-long jest.
